summary: 印度海军已表示有兴趣支持开发旋转爆震发动机（RDE）驱动的超音速海军导弹。该问题陈述是在 2026 年 10 月举行的 Swavlamban 2026 海军旗舰展览期间发布的纲要的一部分，旨在展示国防创新。问题陈述的全文如下：该问题陈述确定了与旋转爆震发动机 (RDE) 研究相关的拟议本土超音速海军导弹计划。 RDE 研究将旋转爆炸作为推进原理。挑战
content:
印度海军已表示有兴趣支持开发旋转爆震发动机（RDE）驱动的超音速海军导弹。该问题陈述是在 2026 年 10 月举行的 Swavlamban 2026 海军旗舰展览期间发布的纲要的一部分，旨在展示国防创新。问题陈述的全文如下：该问题陈述确定了与旋转爆震发动机 (RDE) 研究相关的拟议本土超音速海军导弹计划。 RDE 研究将旋转爆炸作为推进原理。面临的挑战是确定它是否为所述海军应用提供可靠、可支持的能力途径。评估应区分科学可行性、组件成熟度、综合演示准备情况和服务使用资格。需要独立的证据来证实所声称的相对于现有推进替代方案的优势。该计划应在整个评估过程中保持明确的要求、配置控制、专家安全监督和结果的可追溯性。国内设计所有权、制造可重复性、环境适应性和长期支持是核心考虑因素。预期结果是对可行性和成熟度进行基于证据的评估，并得到授权研究和评估的支持。
在其他航空航天应用中取得的进展不应被视为海军导弹已做好准备的证明。燃气轮机和冲压发动机等传统发动机通过亚音速燃烧过程（也称为爆燃）产生推力。爆震发动机利用持续超音速燃烧（也称为爆震）产生的冲击波来产生推力。这意味着，对于相似的尺寸和重量等级，与燃气轮机或冲压发动机相比，爆震发动机不仅可以提供更大的推力，而且可以提供更高的效率。一家名为 D-Propulse Aerospace 的印度初创公司于 2026 年 7 月在 DRDO 测试设施测试了 RDE 原型机，在 24 小时内进行了五次静态测试。 D-Propulse 随后公布了开发 RDE 动力的吸气式超音速巡航导弹和旋转爆震火箭发动机 (RDRE) 动力的微型 SAM 的计划，用于反 UAS 应用。 《海军新闻》联系了创始人兼首席执行官 Saurav Jha，询问该公司对海军问题陈述的看法：D-Propulse 打算利用其吸气式 RDE 技术来制造超音速巡航导弹，这种导弹比传统系统更小、更便宜，但仍能达到作战射程。这将允许迄今为止只能承载距离更短的系统的平台进行承载。较低的价格将使印度军方能够实现真正的大规模精确化。
毕竟，超音速巡航导弹比其他类型的系统到达目标的概率要高得多。因此，超音速巡航导弹的弹匣深度是当今情况下的关键要求，我们的目标价格点应该能够实现这一点。 D-Propulse 的马赫 3 超音速巡航导弹的 CAD 渲染图（图片来自 D-Propulse） 在回答有关与海军就 RDE 海军导弹进行谈判的问题时，Jha 表示，D-Propulse 一直在与相关利益相关者就其正在开发的系统进行磋商，包括通过既定机制寻求支持。在海德拉巴测试的发动机已在 Swavlamban 2026 上展出，是经过验证的发动机

【原文 English Original】
The Indian Navy has expressed interest in supporting the development of a Rotating Detonation Engine (RDE) – powered supersonic naval missile. The problem statement was part of a compendium released during Swavlamban 2026, the Navy’s flagship exhibition meant to showcase defence innovation, held in October 2026. The full text of the problem statement is as follows: This problem statement identifies a proposed indigenous supersonic naval missile programme associated with Rotating Detonation Engine (RDE) research. RDE research examines rotating detonation as a propulsion principle. The challenge is to establish whether it offers a credible, supportable capability pathway for the stated naval application. The assessment should distinguish scientific feasibility, component maturity, integrated demonstrator readiness and qualification for service use. Independent evidence is required to substantiate claimed advantages against established propulsion alternatives. The programme should maintain clear requirements, configuration control, specialist safety oversight and traceability of results throughout its evaluation. Domestic design ownership, manufacturing repeatability, environmental suitability and long-term support are central considerations. The expected outcome is an evidence-based assessment of feasibility and maturity, supported by authorised research and evaluation. Demonstrated progress in another aerospace application should not be treated as proof of readiness for a naval missile. Traditional engines like gas turbines and ramjets generate thrust by subsonic combustion process, also known as deflagration. Detonation engines utilize the shockwaves generated due to sustained supersonic combustion, also known as detonation, to generate thrust. This means that for a similar size and weight class, detonation engines can not only provide greater thrust but also better efficiency compared to gas turbines or ramjets. An Indian startup named D-Propulse Aerospace had tested an RDE prototype at a DRDO test facility in July 2026, conducting five static tests in 24 hours. D-Propulse subsequently unveiled plans to develop RDE powered air-breathing supersonic cruise missiles and rotating detonation rocket engine (RDRE) powered micro-SAMs for counter-UAS applications. Naval News reached out to founder and CEO Saurav Jha to inquire about the firm’s views regarding the Navy’s problem statement: D-Propulse intends to leverage its air-breathing RDE technology to build supersonic cruise missiles that are much smaller and cheaper than legacy systems and yet reach operational ranges. This would allow carriage by platforms that hitherto could only carry much shorter ranged systems. The lower price point will enable true mass in precision for the Indian military. After all, supersonic cruise missiles have a much higher probability of arrival over target than other types of systems out there. So, having magazine depth for supersonic cruise missiles is a key requirement in today’s scenario and our target price point should enable that. CAD Rendering of D-Propulse’s Mach 3 Supersonic Cruise Missile (Image via D-Propulse) In response to a question regarding talks with the Navy for the RDE naval missile, Jha stated that D-Propulse has been in consultation with the relevant stakeholders for the system it is developing, including for support through established mechanisms. The engine tested at Hyderabad was put on display at Swavlamban 2026 and is the proof motor of a flight-capable design. Naval News has learnt that based on that test data, new iterations will be fabricated and tested at the company’s newly constructed large connected-pipe Combustor Test Facility. D-Propulse aims to compress the developmental cycle significantly with this facility and has offered the facility to other small engine developers. Naval News also requested comments from Jha regarding the rationale behind the planned development of the RDRE micro-SAM: The idea behind the RDRE-powered micro SAM is to flip the economics of war in the favour of the defender. RDRE-powered micro-SAMs will be faster and more maneuverable than existing systems, allowing the user to address a wider range of incoming subsonic loitering munitions. Our studies show that RDRE technology can bring down the cost of effective systems greatly, perhaps even to the point of these being seen as ‘consumable ammunition’ if the production runs are large enough. And given the saturation scenarios we are seeing across conflict zones such as the Persian Gulf, where literally thousands of low-RCS subsonic munitions are being lobbed at air defence networks, I believe that our RDRE power counter UAS micro SAM will be required in very significant numbers in the near future. D-Propulse intends to offer the air-breathing RDE powered supersonic cruise missile for user trials by the end of 2029 and intends to offer the RDRE powered micro-SAM by mid-2028. Globally, extensive work is being done in the United States on developing RDE technology. Under the DARPA GAMBIT program, RTX’s Pratt & Whitney had completed a series of RDE tests in 2025. AFRL has also worked on RDE technology and recently expressed interest in combined-cycle RDRE , seeking a flight demonstration to validate the system’s operational viability. GE Aerospace had tested turbine- based combined-cycle RDE in 2023. In January 2026, Lockheed Martin and GE Aerospace demonstrated a liquid fuel RDE for missiles. Venus Aerospace , L3Harris and IN Space LLC are also developing various types of detonation engines. In the Indian context, an RDE powered supersonic missile would be complementary to the BrahMos . While the latter with its proven production run and ever increasing range will remain the mainstay weapon of the Navy, lighter subsonic and supersonic missiles are likely to proliferate due to cost and weight benefits. Missiles like the NASM-SR and NASM-MR are being developed by DRDO. The lighter form factor of an RDE powered naval missile may make it analogous to the BrahMos NG, which is currently in the R&D stage. Dr. Jaiteerth Joshi, CEO of BrahMos Aerospace, recently told ANI that the first model of BrahMos NG is expected by 2029. Once fabricated, several rounds of trials are required before the missile can be inducted. Dr. Joshi also confirmed the development of a 1,500 km ranged version of the BrahMos, up from the current maximum of about 800 km . The range extension will continue to occur in a phased manner and the 1,500 km range version has been designed and is currently undergoing simulations. BrahMos Aerospace has a nearly a full orderbook and continues to bag export orders. After ordering three batteries for $370 million in 2022 , the Philip p ines is reportedly exploring purchase of “at least six additional BrahMos batteries.” India has also offered to explore the integration of BrahMos on Philippine naval vessels. Five Akash SAM regiments and the Pinaka MLRS are also being looked at by the Philippine Marines and Army, Firstpost reported. Earlier, India’s defence secretary had confirmed that initial deals were signed with two more countries in Southeast Asia for the BrahMos. Vietnam is likely to receive a single coastal battery worth about $100 million while Indonesia has signed two $100 million contracts. Both countries are expected to place larger orders in the coming years. Philippine Marines showcase the BrahMos anti-ship missile system for the first time during the service’s 75th anniversary. More on Swavlamban 2026 Other notable firms with flagship projects present at Swavlamban 2026 included: Sagar Defence Engineering which developed the Matangi USV. Sagar Defence has commenced delivery of 12 meter class USVs to the Navy in 2026 after receiving an order for 12 USVs. Xinfinti Aerospace is developing Naval Chetak Autonomous System (NCAS). NCAS is supported by the Navy under iDEX program and seeks to convert HAL Chetak helicopters into uncrewed assets, an endeavor attempted and aborted by a HAL – IAI combine in the 2010s. Kalam Labs has obtained an iDEX contract from the Navy for the development of floating aircraft carriers. Co-founder Ahmed Faraaz told Naval News that the product will be an airship that can transport Kalam Labs’ suite of propeller driven high-altitude proven swarm-capable UAVs to altitudes exceeding 50,0000 feet. The altitude will enable the airship to stay protected from anti-aircraft munitions while conducting ISR and deploying UAVs for various tasks. Kalam Labs has deployed its UAVs from altitudes greater than 100,000 feet using balloons. Faraaz told Naval News that the firm has also bagged iDEX contracts from IAF for development of a supersonic autonomous spaceplane and mesh enabled space drone swarms. （中央社記者葉蓁芸、劉建邦台北20日電）第二場台北市長選舉公辦政見發表會明天下午2時舉行，台北市長蔣萬安將聚焦台北願景；民進黨市長候選人沈伯洋則將講述公務員減壓等政見。
根據北市選委會資料，市長選舉公辦政見發表會共2場，分別於14日、21日下午辦理，2人一組，當天抽籤決定發言順序，每人發言時間30分鐘。
北市選委會表示，21日下午2時5分至下午3時6分由3號沈伯洋、6號唐新民發言；下午3時10分至下午4時11分由4號蕭文乾、5號蔣萬安發言；下午4時15分至下午5時16分則是1號郭璽、2號林志成發言時間。
蔣萬安日前表示，第二場政見會聚焦台北願景，從城市角度向市民報告；沈伯洋則在第一次政見發表會時表示，第二場將講述公務員減壓等政見。
北市選委會指出，依公職人員選舉罷免法、公職人員選舉公辦政見發表會實施辦法規定，並審酌各參選人參加公辦政見發表會意願，市長、議員選舉均採用一輪式辦理公辦政見發表會，透過有線電視系統公用頻道（第3頻道）及YouTube影音平台直播。（編輯：張銘坤）1151120

（中央社記者賴于榛台北20日電）外交部今晚表示，中國官媒新華社在中國與印尼雙邊會談後，報導稱印尼堅定奉行一中政策，但經查證，印尼總統府新聞稿及國務秘書部新聞稿等官方文件均無相關文字內容，報導不實。
中國國家主席習近平今天與印尼總統普拉伯沃（Prabowo Subianto）舉行雙邊會談，新華社在會後報導指稱「印尼堅定奉行一中政策，認為台灣是中華人民共和國的一個省」。
外交部晚間透過新聞稿表示，經查印尼總統府新聞稿及國務秘書部新聞稿等官方文件，均無此等文字內容，顯見新華社相關報導內容不實，外交部予以嚴正駁斥。
外交部說，中國官媒再次以片面之詞企圖替其他國家發言，蓄意矮化台灣主權地位，但無論中國如何散布貶抑中華民國主權的政治敘事，都無法改變中華民國台灣與中華人民共和國互不隸屬，中華民國為主權獨立民主國家的客觀事實。
對於中國官媒類似作法頻傳，外交部表示，國際社會應秉持客觀事實認清中共操弄不實言論伎倆，共同反制此等意圖以政治脅迫與資訊操弄影響國際社會認知的惡劣行徑。（編輯：謝佳珍）1151120

content:
韩联社首尔11月21日电 【要闻回顾】BLACKPINK成员Jennie获两项格莱美提名；韩国演员高庚杓承认醉驾并宣布暂停演艺活动；防弹少年团开启世巡“阿里郎”亚洲及澳大利亚站；NCT DREAM正规六辑销量破百万大关。
女团BLACKPINK成员Jennie凭借与澳大利亚迷幻摇滚乐队Tame Impala合作的歌曲《Dracula》，获得第69届格莱美奖最佳流行对唱/组合表演（最佳流行合作）与年度制作两项提名。其中，年度制作属于格莱美四大通类奖项之一。《Dracula》原曲于去年10月首次发行，今年2月推出Jennie参与的混音版后迅速走红，最高冲至美国公告牌百强单曲榜第三位。
此外，韩国女团IVE和KiiiKiii分别凭借《BANG BANG》和《404 (New Era)》，入围本届新设的“最佳亚洲流行音乐表演”奖。
演员高庚杓15日在其社交账号发文，就醉酒驾车引发交通事故一事道歉，并宣布暂停演艺活动。高庚杓于14日凌晨3时30分许在首尔麻浦区东桥洞酒后驾车，撞上环卫清洁车，当时他的血液酒精浓度达到吊销驾照标准（0.08%及以上）。
高庚杓出演的综艺节目《闲着干嘛呢》《第六感：B Side》《惊人的星期六》有待播出，他出演的《宝剑魔法》第二季和《大逃脱：都市怪谈》分别将于本月29日和下月2日上线。
防弹少年团（BTS）世巡“阿里郎”的亚洲及澳大利亚站演出19日拉开帷幕，整体计划在9座城市共举办26场演出。其中，亚洲站将于11月19日、21日、22日率先在高雄开唱，随后陆续登陆曼谷、吉隆坡、新加坡、雅加达、香港和布拉干，在7座城市共举办21场演唱会；澳大利亚站则将于明年2月在墨尔本和悉尼共举办5场演出。
11月21日的高雄第二场演出和12月29日的雅加达第三场演出将在全球80多个国家和地区的各大院线转播。
经纪公司SM娱乐16日表示，旗下男团NCT DREAM第六张正规专辑《DREAM AFTER DREAM》销量突破百万大关。
《DREAM AFTER DREAM》于本月9日发行。以韩国唱片销售统计网站Hanteo Chart统计为准，该专辑首周销量达到100.25万张，排名周榜第一。这是NCT DREAM自首张正规专辑以来，连续第11张销量突破百万张。该专辑在发行后席卷韩国主要音乐排行榜，还在QQ音乐和酷狗音乐排行榜取得亮眼成绩。

title: Launch Preview: Ariane 6 to launch Amazon satellites, Falcon 9 to launch government missions
zh_title: 发射预览：阿丽亚娜 6 号将发射亚马逊卫星，猎鹰 9 号将发射政府任务

content:
经过一周繁忙的发射活动，本周全球发射清单预计将进行六次发射，其中包括范登堡发射的 3 次 SpaceX 猎鹰 9 号发射任务、中国的两次发射任务以及南美洲的阿丽亚娜 6 号发射任务。 SpaceX 将为美国太空部队和国家侦察办公室发射有效载荷，而本周的中国任务和阿丽亚娜 6 号任务中至少有一次将发射一批互联网卫星。长征2D |有效载荷未知，将于 11 月 18 日星期三从中国发射，长征 2D (CZ-2D) 预计将于世界标准时间 22:50 从太原卫星发射中心的 9 号发射场 (LC-9) 发射。官方警告通知表明发射轨迹是向南的，但有效载荷及其预定轨道的详细信息要等到发射后才会发布。两级、40.77 米高的 CZ-2D 由上海航天技术研究院 (SAST) 制造。 2D 版本不需要额外的捆绑式助推器。此次飞行将是长征2D的第108次飞行，也是今年的第七次。猎鹰 9 号 | USSF-317 (R-6) SpaceX 将于 11 月 18 日星期三进行本周两次发射中的第一次发射，发射时间为四小时，发射窗口于太平洋标准时间晚上 7:00（世界标准时间周四 03:00）开始。
USSF-317 任务是美国太空军 (USSF) 本周的唯一任务，将从加利福尼亚州范登堡太空部队基地 (VSFB) 的东 4 号航天发射场 (SLC-4E) 发射，向东南飞行，将其机密有效载荷送入低地球轨道 (LEO)。所有系统看起来都很好，天气也有利于升空。猎鹰 9 号发射的 USSF-627 任务即将开始从加利福尼亚州发射推进剂 → https://t.co/IdlZbviZZl pic.twitter.com/fKxyN4DIui — SpaceX (@SpaceX) 2026 年 11 月 12 日助推器 B1100 将支持此次任务，这是自近一年前 11 月 23 日首次支持星链集团 11-30 以来的第十一次飞行， 2025 年。除了 NROL-105 和 USSF-385 之外，助推器之前的八次飞行支持了星链任务。 SpaceX 的西海岸无人机飞船 Of Course I Still Love You 将在 B1100 升空后约 8 分钟着陆时驻扎在地面。猎鹰 9 号是一枚直径 3.9 米、高 70 米的两级火箭。九台 Merlin 1D 发动机为第一级助推器提供动力，而第二级则使用一台真空优化的 Merlin 发动机。猎鹰 9 号和猎鹰重型火箭是第一批实现定期重复使用的轨道火箭，其中一枚猎鹰助推器已飞行 37 次。飞行后，两个有效载荷整流罩也被回收并重复使用。长征8A | SatNet LEO Group 本周第二次中国发射计划于 11 月 11 日星期五举行。
世界标准时间 20 日 11:00，在中国文昌航天发射场的商业 LC-1 发射台上发射。长征 8A (CZ-8A) 将携带 9 颗通信卫星进入近地轨道，这些卫星由 SatNet 拥有并由中国卫星网络集团运营。 CZ-8A火箭有两个直径3.35米的级，总高度为50.54 m。第一级由两个捆绑式液体燃料助推器辅助。此次飞行将标志着 CZ-8A 的第 13 次飞行，也是 2026 年的第七次飞行。 NROL-136 SpaceX 本周的第二次猎鹰 9 号任务定于 11 月 21 日星期六太平洋标准时间凌晨 4:30（世界标准时间 12:30）发射，同样是从加州 VSFB 的 SLC-4E 发射。 NROL-136 任务将携带未知数量的有效载荷进入近地轨道，供国家侦察办公室 (NRO) 的增殖建筑星座使用，该星座由 Space 建造

【原文 English Original】
Following a week of busy launch activity, the worldwide launch manifest is set to see six launches this week, with three SpaceX Falcon 9 missions from Vandenberg, two Chinese missions, and an Ariane 6 mission from South America. SpaceX will launch payloads for the United States Space Force and the National Reconnaissance Office, while at least one of this week’s Chinese missions and the Ariane 6 will launch a batch of internet satellites. Chang Zheng 2D | Unknown Payload Wednesday, Nov. 18, will see a launch from China, with a Chang Zheng 2D (CZ-2D) expected to launch from Launch Complex 9 (LC-9) at the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center at 22:50 UTC. Official warning notices indicate a southerly launch trajectory, but details of the payload and its intended orbit will not be released until after launch. The two-stage, 40.77-m-tall CZ-2D is manufactured by the Shanghai Academy of Spaceflight Technology (SAST). The 2D variant requires no additional strap-on boosters. This flight will mark the 108th CZ-2D to fly, the seventh of this year. Falcon 9 | USSF-317 (R-6) SpaceX’s first of two launches this week comes on Wednesday, Nov. 18, at the start of a four-hour launch window that opens at 7:00 PM PST (03:00 UTC on Thursday). The only mission for the United States Space Force (USSF) this week, the USSF-317 mission will launch from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) in California, flying southeast to place its classified payload into low-Earth orbit (LEO). All systems are looking good, and weather is favorable for liftoff. Propellant load is about to begin for Falcon 9’s launch of the USSF-627 mission from California → https://t.co/IdlZbviZZl pic.twitter.com/fKxyN4DIui — SpaceX (@SpaceX) November 12, 2026 Booster B1100 will support this mission, marking its eleventh flight since first supporting Starlink Group 11-30 nearly a year ago on Nov. 23, 2025. Eight of the booster’s previous flights supported Starlink missions, in addition to flying NROL-105 and USSF-385. SpaceX’s west coast droneship, Of Course I Still Love You, will be stationed downrange for B1100’s landing approximately eight minutes after liftoff. Falcon 9 is a 3.9-m-diameter, 70-m-tall two-stage rocket. Nine Merlin 1D engines power the first-stage booster, while the second stage uses a single vacuum-optimized Merlin engine. Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy were the first orbital rockets to achieve regular re-use, with one Falcon booster having flown 37 flights. The two payload fairings are also recovered and reused after flight. Chang Zheng 8A | SatNet LEO Group The second Chinese launch of the week is scheduled for Friday, Nov. 20, at 11:00 UTC from the Commercial LC-1 pad at the Wenchang Space Launch Site in China. A Chang Zheng 8A (CZ-8A) will carry nine communications satellites into LEO, with the satellites owned by SatNet and operated by the China Satellite Network Group. The CZ-8A rocket features two 3.35-m-diameter stages, with a total height of 50.54 m. The first stage is assisted by two strap-on liquid-fuelled boosters. This flight will mark the 13th overall CZ-8A flight, the seventh of 2026. Falcon 9 | NROL-136 SpaceX’s second Falcon 9 mission of the week is scheduled to launch on Saturday, Nov. 21, at 4:30 AM PST (12:30 UTC), again from SLC-4E at VSFB in California. The NROL-136 mission will carry an unknown number of payloads into LEO for the National Reconnaissance Office’s (NRO) Proliferated Architecture constellation, built by SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The booster supporting this mission will be B1097, flying for the 14th time. This booster first flew on Sept. 3, 2025, and has previously flown eight Starlink missions, as well as NROL-172, Transporter 17, Sentinel-6B, Twilight (Pandora & Others), and USSF-259. Following stage separation, B1097 will conduct a return-to-launch-site landing at Landing Zone 4 (LZ-4), located directly next to SLC-4E. Ariane 64 | Amazon Leo (LE-04) Amazon is continuing to put together its constellation of Leo satellites and will add another 36 on Monday, Nov. 23, at 10:12 UTC aboard an Ariane 64. The rocket will launch from Ensemble de Lancement Ariane 4 (ELA-4) at the Guiana Space Centre in French Guiana, with the launch window lasting five hours and 27 minutes. Ariane 64 will follow a northeastern trajectory, delivering 22,000 kg of Leo satellites into LEO. Ariane 64 is a 62-m-tall, 5.4-m-diameter, expendable two-stage rocket built by the ArianeGroup on behalf of the European Space Agency. Both stages are powered by liquid hydrogen and oxygen-fuelled engines. The 64 variant of the basic Ariane 6 utilizes four P129 strap-on solid rocket boosters to provide additional lift-off thrust. This will be the fifth Ariane 6 mission of 2026. Watch the full replay of #VA269 . Relive Ariane 6's successful mission carrying 36 Amazon Leo satellites into orbit. First flight with P160C boosters Heaviest Ariane payload ever #LaunchingAmbitions #Ariane6 #VA269 @Amazonleo @ArianeGroup @esa @CNES @EuropeSpacePort pic.twitter.com/YLxW60wAo1 — Arianespace (@Arianespace) June 17, 2026 Falcon 9 | USSF-266 (TH-3) Closing out the week, a Falcon 9 launch is currently scheduled for Monday, Nov. 23, at 8:04 AM PST (16:04 UTC) — the third this week from SLC-4E at VSFB. The classified USSF-266 mission has a four-hour launch window extending to 12:04 PM PST (20:04 UTC). Falcon 9 will fly due south, indicating a polar orbit for the payload. While the payload is classified, the launch trajectory and other factors suggest that this may be an additional batch of satellites for the USSF’s Space-Based Airborne Moving Target Indicator (SB-AMTI) program. These are based on the SpaceX Starshield satellite bus. The Falcon 9 booster supporting this flight will be B1081, making its 29th flight. B1081 first flew on Aug. 26, 2023, and flew four missions from SpaceX’s Florida launch sites before moving to Vandenberg for Transporter 10, where it has operated since then. The booster will land atop Of Course I Still Love You , stationed approximately 640 km downrange in the Pacific Ocean. If the current schedule holds, this will mark the 122nd Falcon 9 flight of 2026, and the 273rd orbital launch attempt worldwide in 2026. (Lead Image: Falcon 9 launches into the Florida morning skies. Credit: Julia Bergeron for NSF) The post Launch Preview: Ariane 6 to launch Amazon satellites, Falcon 9 to launch government missions appeared first on NASASpaceFlight.com .
